Useful proof structure in the supplied candidate: for a and b, split by parity. Opposite parity makes the relevant numerator factors and H,D odd, giving 2-adic valuation −3 for each coordinate. If m,n are odd, v₂(H)=1, v₂(D)≥3, and both m²−7n² and 7m²−n² have valuation 1, again giving negative valuations. These factors cannot vanish because that would make 7 or 1/7 a rational square. For c, H±D=2m²,2n²>0 imply 0<|D|<H, hence 0<|c|<8/9. For e, integrality would imply H divides its numerator; reducing that numerator modulo H gives 32n⁴. Since gcd(H,n)=1 this forces H|32, whereas H has 2-adic valuation 0 or 1 and H≥5.

For the f,g claims, the candidate establishes Q>0, v₂(Q)∈{0,2}, and v₃(Q)∈{0,2}. Thus if Q had no prime divisor above 3 it would divide 36; the assumptions imply Q≥153, a contradiction. These imply vₚ(f)=−2vₚ(Q); substitution f(−m,n)=g(m,n) yields the same result for g. Finally, in Fₚ the elements r=D/(6mn), s=H/(4mn) satisfy r²=−1 and s²=−2. Setting z=(s/r)(1+r)/2 gives z²=r and z⁴=−1, so z has order 8 and p≡1 mod 8. problem_contract.statement: For coprime integers m,n with n>0, mn≠0, and m²≠n², put H=m²+n², D=m²−n², and Q=m⁴+34m²n²+n⁴. Define a=−9H/(8D), b=(m²−7n²)H(7m²−n²)/(8D³), c=8D³/(9H³), e=−2(m²+5n²)(5m²+n²)/(9DH), f=−2mn(m²−4mn−3n²)(3m²−4mn−n²)(m³+8m²n+5mn²+4n³)(4m³−5m²n+8mn²−n³)/(DHQ²), and g=2mn(m²+4mn−3n²)(3m²+4mn−n²)(m³−8m²n+5mn²−4n³)(4m³+5m²n+8mn²+n³)/(DHQ²). Then none of a,b,c,e,f,g is an integer. Moreover, Q has a prime divisor p>3; every prime p>3 dividing Q satisfies p≡1 (mod 8) and vₚ(f)=vₚ(g)=−2vₚ(Q).
